clue.text: Wave line in front of fish heading off

indicators.note: a word whose head comes off loses its opening letter

parts.note: a brand is a line of goods sold under one name
taken as written, then losing its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone at the fishmonger's waving at the queue in front of a headless fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In front of' puts the first piece before the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To brandish something is to flourish or shake it about, often a weapon held aloft.

clue.text: Manage to sit next to bishop at church meal

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to run a business is to manage it
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone contriving to sit beside the bishop at a church lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishop's letter comes first, with the run sitting next to it and the church after.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunch is a late-morning repast combining breakfast and lunch.

clue.text: Pal in trouble with mob affected calmness

indicators.note: something in trouble is in disarray, so its letters are thrown out of order
affected means acted upon and altered, so these letters change their arrangement too

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A friend in trouble with a gang, who puts on a show of being calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affected' reads as an adjective on calmness, but it works with 'in trouble' to stir all six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Aplomb is self-possession and composure under pressure, a steady poise.

clue.text: Daughter's 16 on day sweetheart split

parts.note: D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
read as one and six in Roman numerals, I and VI
D is the abbreviation for day
read as sweet-heart, the heart or central letter of sweet

explanation.surface: A daughter turning sixteen splits from her sweetheart on that very day.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is reading 16 not as XVI but digit by digit, 1 then 6, in Roman numerals. Sweetheart splits as the heart of sweet. The 's is 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide something is to separate it into parts, the same verb as split.

clue.text: Women's Institute on beach has endless box of butties

indicators.note: without an end, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a beach is made of sand
WI is the usual abbreviation for the Women's Institute, a British community organisation for women
a chest is a large box, here losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Members of the Women's Institute picnicking on the beach with a cool box of sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the institute after the beach in this down light. Butty is northern British slang for a sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: Butties is informal British slang for sandwiches, especially filled rolls of bread.

clue.text: Fine crab's roaming island tucking into stuff

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine on pencils

indicators.note: to tuck into is to go inside, so one piece is placed within another
a creature roaming wanders about, so the letters wander into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A fine crab wandering across an island, tucking into whatever it finds.
explanation.walkthrough: The island letter goes inside the rearranged crab, near its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff as a noun is cloth or material, the same as fabric.

clue.text: Mount Etna's bound to have deer

indicators.note: to mount is to climb, and in a down light climbing means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the Sicilian volcano, read upwards
to lope is to run with long bounding strides

explanation.surface: Climbing Mount Etna is bound to bring you face to face with deer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like part of the volcano's name, but in a down clue it means climb, so the name is read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Loosely, an antelope is a deer-like grazing animal; the setter uses deer as a broad name for it.

clue.text: Idyllic old Italian metropolis briefly recollected

indicators.note: re-collected means gathered up again, so the letters are reassembled in a new order
said briefly, a word is cut short and loses its last letter

parts.note: an ancient Roman was an old Italian
a metropolis is a big city, cut short

explanation.surface: Fond memories of an idyllic old Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recollected' reads as remembered, but splits as re-collected: gathered up again in a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Romantic describes something idealised and charming, much like a picture-perfect idyllic scene.

clue.text: Spoiled rotten coeds take over group

indicators.note: to take over is to swallow up, so one part encloses the other
something rotten has broken down and decayed, so its letters fall into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a set is a group of things or people

explanation.surface: Spoilt-rotten female students muscling in to take charge of a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoiled rotten' looks like one phrase, but it splits: the definition, then the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosseted means pampered and indulged, treated with excessive care, as a spoiled child is.

clue.text: Lounge endlessly redone to keep French wine cold

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one part is held inside the other
a room redone is rearranged, so these letters are rearranged as well
without an end, the word drops its final letter

parts.note: taken as written, then losing its final letter
vin is the French word for wine

explanation.surface: A lounge being refurbished so that French wine can be stored cool in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold' looks like it describes the wine, but it is the definition, in its sense of unfeeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold in the emotional sense means lacking affection or warmth towards others.

clue.text: Walks angrily and halts in a mile

indicators.note: a thing placed in another sits inside it, so one part goes within the other

parts.note: to halt is to stop
M is the abbreviation for mile

explanation.surface: A hiker storming off in a temper, then stopping after a mile.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomp is to tread heavily and noisily, typically to show annoyance or rage.

clue.text: Most of farce has now gone into decline

indicators.note: most but not all of a word means dropping its final letter

parts.note: a farce is a broad comedy, here losing its last letter

indicators.note: gone in the sense of gone wrong or gone off, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A farce that has now fallen into decline, its glory days gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gone' as in gone wrong signals the shuffle of the short word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedown is a loss of status or fortune, a fall from a higher position.

clue.text: Take a breather during exercise dive

indicators.note: something happening during another falls within it, so one part sits inside

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
a lung is the organ one breathes with

explanation.surface: An instruction to pause for a breath in the middle of a diving workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A breather' looks like a rest, but here it is the thing that breathes.
explanation.definitionFit: A plunge is a sudden headlong dive into water, so the noun and verb both match.

clue.text: What to say on meeting an awkward situation?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the formal greeting when introduced
second meaning: a fine mess, a tricky state of affairs

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes it look like advice for a social gaffe; the same phrase is both a greeting and, as a noun, a pickle.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a formal greeting, and in British informal speech 'a fine how-do-you-do' is an embarrassing mess.

clue.text: Calm cop's ruffled by cool partner in crime

indicators.note: ruffled means disturbed and messed up, so the preceding letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
ice is cool, and to ice is to chill

explanation.surface: A calm police officer rattled by a cool-headed criminal sidekick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' simply places the cool piece beside the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An accomplice is someone who helps another commit an offence, a criminal collaborator.

clue.text: Leaders of Sao Paulo race given bottled Tizer to drink

indicators.note: the leaders of a group of words are their opening letters

parts.note: the opening letters of these three words

indicators.note: bottled is slang for drunk, and drunk letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: Tizer is a British fizzy soft drink, taken as written then rearranged

explanation.surface: Runners in a São Paulo race handed bottles of fizzy pop to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottled' reads as put in bottles, but here it is slang for drunk, so the soft drink's letters stagger.
explanation.definitionFit: A spritzer is a drink of wine mixed with soda water, a long refreshing beverage.

clue.text: Not scared when embroiled in a fraud

indicators.note: embroiled means thrown into confusion, so the following letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A bold swindler who keeps their nerve while caught up in a scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Embroiled in' looks like one phrase, but only the first word is the signal; 'in' joins the letters being mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Unafraid means fearless, showing no fright or anxiety in the face of danger.

clue.text: Spring flower initially planted in front of border came up

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word beside it

parts.note: the opening letter of planted
a rim is an edge or border
rose is the past tense of rise, to come up

explanation.surface: A spring bulb planted at the front of the flower border has come up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Border' sounds like a garden bed, but it means an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The primrose is a pale yellow wild flower that blooms early in spring.

clue.text: Letter-writers' enclosure with note has one in tears

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals
F is a musical note
to rend is to tear apart
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A correspondent's letter arrives with a note that leaves the reader in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' suggests crying, but it is the verb to rip.
explanation.definitionFit: Penfriends are people who keep up a friendship by exchanging letters, usually overseas.

clue.text: Modern weapon disheartened old Japanese dictator

indicators.note: losing heart means losing the central letter of the word

parts.note: a shotgun is a firearm, modern compared with a sword

explanation.surface: A Japanese warlord of old dismayed by the arrival of firearms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' reads as dismayed, but it means losing the central letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A shogun was a hereditary military ruler of Japan, the real power behind the emperor.

clue.text: Alcoholics Anonymous name spirit involved in heart disease

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be inside it, so these pieces go within another

parts.note: AA is the usual abbreviation for Alcoholics Anonymous
N is the abbreviation for name
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A recovering drinker whose spirit habit has led to a heart condition.
explanation.walkthrough: The name and the spirit go together inside the two letters of the support group.
explanation.definitionFit: Angina is chest pain caused by restricted blood supply to the heart muscle, a cardiac condition.

clue.text: Broadcast Madrid team bagging victory in Europe

indicators.note: to bag something is to capture it, holding it inside

parts.note: Real Madrid is the Spanish football club
VE Day marked victory in Europe in 1945

explanation.surface: A sports report on the Madrid side winning a European trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' looks like a noun for a TV report, but it is the verb to make public.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast news is to make it widely known, just as to reveal is to disclose it.

clue.text: Shame main performance involves female unknown

indicators.note: involves means takes in or includes, so one piece is held inside
a performance puts on a new show, so the word before it is reworked

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
F is the abbreviation for female
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns

explanation.surface: A shameful lead performance by an unknown actress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main performance' reads like a headline act, but 'performance' signals the word before it being reworked.
explanation.definitionFit: Infamy is disgrace or notoriety from wicked conduct, public dishonour.

clue.text: Unexpectedly picked up bargain opportunity

indicators.note: picked up as on a radio or by the ear, so a word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a bargain is a good buy
a chance is an opportunity

explanation.surface: Stumbling across a bargain unexpectedly while out shopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' reads as bought, but means heard, so only the first piece changes its spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Done by chance means happening accidentally, without planning or foresight.

clue.text: Partisan's often beyond Zimbabwe's borders

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its edges, its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of Zimbabwe
a lot means often, frequently

explanation.surface: A political supporter who often travels across Zimbabwe's frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beyond' puts the second piece after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealot is a fanatical, uncompromising supporter of a cause, an extreme partisan.

clue.text: Some paper's covering annual meeting in Slough

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so one piece goes outside the other

parts.note: a quire is a set quantity of paper, 24 or 25 sheets
AGM is an annual general meeting

explanation.surface: A local newspaper covering a company's annual meeting held in Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is an English town west of London, but here it is a common noun: a swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a marshy hollow or bog, and a quagmire is soft boggy ground.

clue.text: I'm not sure following fish is a way to steer boat!

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the piece before this word is placed second

parts.note: the rudd is a freshwater fish
er is the hesitant noise of uncertainty

explanation.surface: An angler doubtfully wondering if following the fish is how to steer the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' places the hesitation after the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A rudder is the hinged blade at the stern that a helmsman uses to direct a vessel.

clue.text: Precipitation from pillow failure?

parts.note: pillows are stuffed with soft feathers
a fall from power is a failure

explanation.surface: Feathers drifting from a burst pillow, a little comic disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failure' looks like the definition, since the answer commonly means ruin; but here it is wordplay, and the definition is the weather sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A downfall is also a heavy fall of rain or snow, an older meteorological sense.
